node.statement: Challenge disposition (blocking, not a proof of the parent). The objection is correct. In def-routef-raw-factor-setting, I_B denotes the identity map of B, so the unit element must instead be denoted e_B (or by an unsubscripted I forced by B-element type); thus v(I_B) in the parent is itself ill-typed. More fundamentally, the registered def-extended-delta-inclusion only says that every amplification is a delta-homomorphism and obeys two-sided norm bounds, while no permitted definition or external specifies any base delta-homomorphism clause. Consequently the needed estimate ||v(e_B)-I_A||<=delta cannot be inferred. This is not a merely omitted algebraic bridge: with eta=0, H=C, Phi=id, tilde-Phi=id, A=B=C, v=-id and u=-id, all explicitly stated linear, bijective, inverse, idempotence, extended-0-C*-algebra, and amplification norm conditions hold; because the base predicate is unconstrained by the registered inputs, it may be interpreted as true for these maps, yet ||v(1)-1||=2 while C_T*eta=0. Therefore node 1.2 and hence the unit proof cannot be validated until the pending request fac57c5a9b1c5586 is provisioned with an allowed byte-verbatim definition (or an allowed external) explicitly giving the unit-defect clause; after provisioning, the repaired branch must use e_B and the estimate delta=C_E*epsilon_AI(eta)<=bar C_E*C_A*eta=C_V*eta<=C_T*eta.
